### Executive Summary
Winona County was impacted by back-to-back ransomware attacks in 2026. Following the incidents, the county paid a total of $128,000 to the threat actors involved.

Preliminary information indicates that sensitive personally identifiable information (PII), specifically Social Security numbers, may have been exposed or placed at risk during the unauthorized access.

The incident involved consecutive ransomware deployments affecting Winona County's IT infrastructure. Detailed technical analysis regarding the specific ransomware strain or lateral movement techniques has not yet been confirmed.

The exact root cause and initial access vector used by the attackers remain unconfirmed in the provided source material. The potential compromise of Social Security numbers indicates that threat actors likely gained unauthorized access to internal file stores or administrative databases.

### Mitigation & IOCs
Specific remediation actions and technical mitigations implemented by Winona County were not detailed in the available report. Standard post-ransomware mitigations typically involve isolated system restoration from verified backups, comprehensive credential resets, and endpoint isolation.
